clue.text: Doing nothing popular could be irate

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: could be says the letters of irate can turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone idle and well liked might nonetheless be angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popular' looks like it describes the idler, but it gives IN; 'could be' signals the anagram of IRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a state of inactivity or sluggishness, of not doing anything.

clue.text: Propose to popular nurse

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to tend a patient is to nurse them

explanation.surface: A man asks a much-liked nurse to marry him.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose a course of action is to plan or mean to carry it out.

clue.text: Captivate in umpteenth rally

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words umpteenth rally, running across the word gap

explanation.surface: Keep a crowd spellbound at yet another political rally.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone is to hold them spellbound, to enchant them.

clue.text: Canine trouble?

parts.note: reads as a dog's problem, but a canine is also a pointed tooth, so the trouble is pain in it

explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the pointed teeth, so pain there is dental ache.

clue.text: Racially prejudiced against note penned by rising names

parts.note: anti means opposed to or against

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the note goes inside the other piece
in a down clue rising means the word is read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention, so names gives cites
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a document written by people who are climbing the social ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' works only on the CITES piece, giving SETIC, which then encloses MI; the definition is the opening two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or prejudice towards Jewish people as a race is the sense of this word.

clue.text: Passage of handwriting Paul's powerless to translate

parts.note: fist is an informal word for a person's handwriting

indicators.note: to translate is to turn into another form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
P is the abbreviation for power, so powerless means the P is dropped

parts.note: the name Paul, the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A piece of Paul's handwriting is too feeble to be translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' removes P, leaving AUL for 'to translate' to rearrange. 'Passage' is a medical sense: a channel in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A fistula is an abnormal channel in the body connecting two organs or an organ and the skin.

clue.text: Appropriate measure taken about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the measure goes around the one

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot, a measure of length
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A suitable step is taken regarding a single issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit is suitable, right for the purpose.

clue.text: Fibre chewed by Lassie endlessly

indicators.note: something chewed is mangled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the final letter of Lassie is cut off

explanation.surface: Some string has been gnawed by the famous collie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LASSIE to LASSI, and 'chewed' rearranges it. Lassie is the collie of the films.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre made from agave leaves, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Peace-keepers never having potential to disarm

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peace-keeping forces

indicators.note: having potential suggests the letters of never could become something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: United Nations troops never seem able to strip fighters of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having potential' rearranges NEVER into NERVE. 'disarm' here means to unsettle someone, not to remove weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone can mean to throw them off balance, to rattle their composure.

clue.text: Unusual stance taken over railway line

indicators.note: in a down clue taken over means placed above, so the anagram comes before the railway
unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters of stance are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd position is adopted above a railway track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' here means family descent, not a railway line, despite the railway in the clue. 'Unusual' signals the anagram, giving ANCEST.
explanation.definitionFit: One's line is one's lineage, the family descent from forebears.

clue.text: Popular version of lex talionis

parts.note: lex talionis is the Latin law of retaliation, an eye for an eye; the popular version is the everyday phrase for paying back like with like

explanation.definitionFit: The everyday phrase means retaliating in kind, the same principle as the ancient law of retribution.

clue.text: Icons for generating sound

indicators.note: generating means producing something new, so the letters of icons are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Religious images are used to produce noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is an adjective meaning relating to sound or sound waves.

clue.text: Thorn growing in Arctic?

indicators.note: growing means developing into something else, so the letters of thorn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prickly plant is somehow surviving in the frozen far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing' rearranges THORN. The question mark marks the definition as an example: the Arctic lies at the top of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is the polar region at the top of the world, an example of the compass point direction.

clue.text: Minor members' colts?

definitions.meaning: minor members read as little limbs, belonging to someone
Colts are revolvers made by the Colt company, not young horses

explanation.surface: Junior club members own some young horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Small limbs fit the first reading; the second is handguns and rifles, firearms carried by hand, like Colt revolvers.

clue.text: Magic word makes rotter confined by a pair of supports

indicators.note: confined by means shut inside, so the rotter is placed within the pair
a pair of means the piece made from a and supports is used twice

parts.note: a bra is a support garment
a cad is a rotter, an ungentlemanly man

explanation.surface: A conjuror's spell makes a scoundrel trapped between two props.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' are bras, not props; 'a pair of' doubles A BRA, giving ABRAABRA for the rotter to split.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjuror's incantation, the classic spell said when performing a trick.

clue.text: Ban pro European crook?

parts.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it, as a trade union might
a marketeer was a supporter of Britain joining the European Common Market

explanation.surface: A ban is imposed on a crooked supporter of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: MARKETEER dates from the debates over Britain joining the Common Market.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who trades illegally in scarce goods is a kind of criminal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: English funny men kept on for course of study

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so on goes within the funny men

parts.note: comics are comedians, funny men
taken as written

explanation.surface: English comedians were retained for a university subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' is the container signal: 'kept on' sounds like retained, but here the word ON is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of production, wealth and trade is an academic discipline taught at university.

clue.text: Time for cocoa is organised at noon

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters of cocoa and is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinks break is arranged for midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' signals the anagram of COCOA IS, giving OCCASIO; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular moment or instance when something happens.

clue.text: Electricity bill and the means to pay it?

parts.note: an electric current is the flow of electricity
an account is a bill for goods or services

explanation.surface: An electricity bill arrives along with the way to settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: An everyday bank arrangement from which bills are paid by cheque or debit.

clue.text: Fence on right is showing signs of weakness

parts.note: ailing means unwell, showing signs of weakness

explanation.surface: A fence on the right-hand side is starting to sag.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier of rails or bars is a kind of fence.

clue.text: Having zero potential for being worthy of remark

definitions.meaning: read as two words: incapable, with no ability

explanation.surface: Being capable of nothing is a reason to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the letters mean incapable; whole, they mean noteworthy or distinguished.

clue.text: Swear when getting nothing for pudding?

indicators.note: getting means taking in, so the curse receives the nothing inside it

parts.note: to curse is to swear
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone swears when there is no dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' puts O inside CURSE. The question mark shows pudding is an example: dessert is one part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is one stage of a meal, an example of a dinner's successive dishes.

clue.text: I moan about tart, an essential part of diet

indicators.note: about means around in a jumbled way, so the letters of I moan are rearranged

parts.note: acid means sharp or sour, tart in taste

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a sour pastry being a key part of their meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I MOAN into AMINO, followed by ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the building blocks of protein, some of which must come from food.

clue.text: Players of note appearing in part of autumn briefly

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so the note goes within the month
briefly means in short form, so the month's name is cut down to its usual three-letter abbreviation

parts.note: October is a month that falls in autumn
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Musicians of distinction perform during a short autumn stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the month to OCT. 'Players of note' looks like one phrase meaning distinguished performers, but 'of' is a link and 'note' gives TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians performing together.

clue.text: Unfashionable party's best

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A dowdy gathering is still the finest one around.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat or surpass them; here best is a verb.

clue.text: One point about one fool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the point goes around the second one

parts.note: a dot is a point
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single person argues a point about one silly fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside DOT, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person, a nitwit.

clue.text: General prohibition might close this down?

parts.note: public means general, shared by all
a bar is a ban or prohibition

explanation.surface: A nationwide ban on drink could shut a pub room.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with the whole clue: Prohibition, a general ban on alcohol, would shut a drinking room.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain drinking room in a British pub would close if alcohol were prohibited.

clue.text: Talk complainingly over remuneration

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to yap is to talk noisily and complainingly

explanation.surface: Someone moans endlessly about their wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration is money received for work, wages or salary.

clue.text: Eve comes thus gallantly, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is said aloud, a sound-alike

parts.note: a knight behaves chivalrously, so knightly means gallantly

explanation.surface: Eve arrives with a gentleman's courtesy, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve here is evening, which arrives every night. KNIGHTLY has a silent K.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening arrives every night, so it comes on a daily-after-dark basis.

clue.text: Severe wind to East

parts.note: Auster is the south wind, from the Latin name

explanation.surface: A harsh wind blows towards the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster was the Roman god of the south wind; the name is used for the wind itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern and strict, plain and harsh.
